term: Jesus' giving a power (Commissioning.Gave) and governing power (Power.Governing)
definition: Commissioning.Gave p: Jesus himself gave or promised the power p to one or more of his disciples or to their community (Matthew 18.17 assigns judging to the ekklēsia). It is an uninterpreted event parameter of the Commissioning structure, distinct from any report; the type does not tie it to the signature's jesus, so its reading as Jesus' act is this definition's. GoesBackToJesus E r: Jesus gave or promised every power that report r names (CommissionReport.powers). Power.Governing: a power is governing when its exercise is authority over the members of a society: holding the keys, binding and loosing, the church's judging and excluding, forgiving and retaining sins, shepherding the flock. Preaching, making disciples, baptizing and teaching are not governing. The power list also contains preaching, the commission Harnack names.
note: Stipulative modelling choice for #357, not a sourced reading. The classification is chosen so that a commission consisting only of proclaiming, discipling, baptizing and teaching stays compatible with the message rival (a movement may preach, teach and baptize without a governing structure); counting teaching or baptizing as governing would make the rival's Matthew 28 concession already institutional and so would beg the question. Lumen gentium §§19-20 and 25-27 (teaching, sanctifying, governing) would be a source for a finer division; Gave counts a promise (Matthew 16.19) as giving, a choice the report claim for Matthew 16 records. The record covers Commissioning.Gave and GoesBackToJesus as well as its named lean_declaration Power.Governing.
